reviews.text: Baker’s brave and bracing film is far from a whimsical fable.  It is a dramatic thumbnail depiction of a growing section of this nation’s culture that many may not want to admit exists, let alone condone.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: Baker's vision for The Florida Project is brilliant in concept and even more vital in execution. The ending to this film is easily some of the best filmmaking of 2017.
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: Its potent combination of empathy, observation and miraculously natural performances make this a modern classic, with strong echoes of Ken Loach's very best work.
reviews.author: Trevor Johnston

reviews.text: Coupled with Alexis Zabe’s vividly ironic cinematography, and a supporting performance by Willem Dafoe as perhaps a failed parent in his own way, and The Florida Project is nothing short of authentic perfection...
reviews.author: Brendan Cassidy

reviews.text: It’s superficially less bleak than Tangerine, rendered by Baker in tropical colours, but poverty lurks throughout.
reviews.author: Ed Potton

reviews.text: The charm, wrenching emotion, and compassion that Baker finds in his characters are enhanced by his unique touches of humor and unlikely optimism.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The Florida Project is a rainbow in a rainstorm  illuminating the nuances of life that consume us all, no matter where we live, how much money we make, what our social status is, how we choose to spend our time and who we spend it with.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Baker clearly loves every single person he puts inside his camera and feeds off their nasty wise humor of the doomed... The Florida Project is deeply honest
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: The folks in these stories might be poor, desperate and often completely out of their minds, but there is a curious species of warmth, compassion and even honour in their worlds.
reviews.author: Dorothy Woodend

reviews.text: The best picture of 2017, with Willem Dafoe delivering the performance of the year.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: This movie really challenged me to look at my own compassion.
reviews.author: Hosea Rupprecht

reviews.text: It's a story about poverty that neither celebrates or condemns its characters. Mooney's exploits are entertaining and yet an air of jeopardy hangs heavy over every minute of the movie.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: With a deeply moving emotional current, The Florida Project fictionally portrays a growing marginalized section of the American population.
reviews.author: Joanne Laurier

reviews.text: The Florida Project manages to surpass Tangerine by displaying an even broader social frieze. And all the characters, even the most insignificant, have their two or three seconds of dignity [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Agustín Acevedo Kanopa

reviews.text: Fizzing with vitality, brimful of empathy and insight.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: It's not attempting to push a narrative as much as it aims to highlight a subsection of society that rarely makes its way onto the big screen.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: It follows not only their adorable adventures during summer break but also the hardships of poverty in modern America.
reviews.author: Film Companion Staff

reviews.text: One of 2017's most outstanding cinematic achievements.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: [S]ome of the most heartbreaking, affirming filmmaking in recent memory, the kind only achieved by a director with the utmost sympathy for their characters.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: As Hally digs herself a hole time and time again, and as the inevitable finally catches up with her and her daughter, we deeply feel for Moonie and her well-being.
reviews.author: Dustin Chang

reviews.text: It's ironic, living so close to the 'Happiest place on Earth', but having to fight for your survival every day. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: A picture of people barely holding, who are complex and damaged, but look out for one another when no one else will. Real and raw, crushing and beautiful, and a scathing indictment of capitalism and a system that treats people as disposable
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: But it's the elevation of the source material into such a delicate yet layered narrative that evinces true artistry.
reviews.author: CJ Sheu

reviews.text: Baker encloses a relevant social commentary about inequality on the darker sides of a castle of innocence, which is undoubtedly its strongest point, but the plot feels a little silly. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Baker makes films like no one else, and they are as vital to understanding America as anything you'll see in this or most other years. It will win you with compassion and warmth, while simultaneously shaking you to your core.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Keenly observational and heart-wrenchingly real. The young actors steal the show in this guy-wrenching drama.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Sean Baker's latest is an achievement in empathy.
reviews.author: Aly Caviness

reviews.text: The Florida Project is just like Moonee and her mother - loud, confident and brutally honest. An explosion of vivid colours, creative camerawork and amazing performances, it is one of the most engaging films this year.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: What sets this film apart is that director Baker does a great job of presenting these characters in an unjaundiced, authentic way.
reviews.author: Leslie Combemale

reviews.text: The scenes feel and most likely are improvised, giving them a sizzling energy that (often literally) screams authenticity and speaks volumes about the protagonists' furiously nomadic way of life.
reviews.author: Zhuo-Ning Su

reviews.text: This is a slice of life many would rather not see, but seeing Willem DaFoe interact with the raw talent in this raw drama makes for worthy viewing.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: This drama provides so many emotional sucker punches. Like Moonlight, it shows, rather than tells, the beautiful, real, and raw story of everyday Americans.
reviews.author: Debbie Holloway

reviews.text: Despite the seeming hopelessness of their tragic situation, the children of The Florida Project are mostly full of precocious joy.
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: It's the kind of ending that hits you like a ton of bricks.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: A bittersweet point of view exercise capable of softening hearts with the greatest tenderness and, at the same time, tearing them apart. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: It might rip your guts to shreds just a little bit, but it'll be worth it.
reviews.author: D. Patrick Rodgers

reviews.text: My #1 movie of 2017
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: A warm, winning, heartbreaking, and deeply moving portrait of those for whom the childlike wonder and happiness that Disney World represents is always in sight, but forever out of reach.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: The Florida Project is sweet, funny, and extremely easy to lose yourself in.
reviews.author: Deirdre Molumby

reviews.text: An exploration of decadence in American culture. As beautiful as it is tragic.
reviews.author: C.H. Newell

reviews.text: A marvel of kid acting, or lack thereof, Sean Baker's touching film about children living a dangerous, hardscrabble existence within spitting distance of Disney World does double duty as entertainment and as a serious social statement.
reviews.author: Julie Crawford

reviews.text: Much like life, The Florida Project is dark yet fun, joyous yet devastating, but, above all, one of the year's absolute finest films.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: ... mirrors the immaturity, irresponsibility, and rudeness of a lost person, whose terrible example for her child, both behavioral and language-wise, is sad and vexatious.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: A sumptuously shot, 35-mm experience that feels utterly lived-in and real, but never loses its cinematic verve; it's a film that will stay with you.
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: A modest miracle of a film, in which director Baker gracefully juggles the story's disparate temperaments.
reviews.author: Andrew Wyatt

reviews.text: The improvisation, accompanied by the boisterous and happy attitudes of the children, endows the film with a touching tone that loads of meaning the gravity of the reflections that sustain it. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: David Poireth

reviews.text: Like American Honey, what The Florida Project manages to do so well is capture the small joys that come with life on the poverty line.
reviews.author: Hannah Ryan

reviews.text: Throughout this two hour visual verite feast, you'll be hit with moments of joy and sadness, inspiration and despondency, and a cinematic romanticism so riveting that you just can't tear yourself away.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: The Florida Project knocks down invisible dividing walls and tries to build empathetic connections between disparate human worlds in a way only cinema can.
reviews.author: Joel Mayward

reviews.text: The Florida Project is both bleak and inspiring as it does its best to reveal the reality inherent in living in dire poverty. It plunges the viewer into its world and never lets up on showing the highs and the lows with brutal clarity.
reviews.author: Kt Schaefer

reviews.text: A powerful punch of empathic, humanist, character-driven cinema.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: If Tangerine was Baker's breakthrough film, then this just cements his status as one of the best young filmmakers in Hollywood today.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: The film never exploits its characters' lives, but simply understands them and, in turn, portrays them both sensitively and candidly.
reviews.author: Kyle Kizu

reviews.text: [These children] don't quite comprehend their parents' struggle or the life of excess and entertainment down the road. They simply find the joy and fun in what they have.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: What bothered me about this (and I ended up loving it) is that the kids are terrible.
reviews.author: Ben Mankiewicz

reviews.text: I knew form the first shot that I was watching a truly great movie... It's so real, it's so raw.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: There's fascinating stories here and it is, at a meta level, almost heartbreaking, almost infuriating that we know that this is a slice of our population that lives this way and doesn't seem to have any other options.
reviews.author: Matt Atchity

reviews.text: An exercise in empathy and exuberance.
reviews.author: Eli Glasner

reviews.text: A powerfully moving dramady by Sean Baker who came a long way from filming a movie off an iPhone.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: I believe The Florida Project is a film with good intentions even though I remain unsure what they are.
reviews.author: Jourdain Searles

reviews.text: Moonee is somehow relentlessly entertaining without ever, even in the slightest bit, coming across like a child mascot dreamed up solely for our amusement.
reviews.author: Adam Epstein

reviews.text: Newcomer Brooklynn Prince is pure magic; a firecracker of intensity and confidence, this girl is a star.
reviews.author: Erik Anderson

reviews.text: A work that combines boundless energy and childlike enthusiasm with dark social realism, Sean Baker's wildly inventive style of filmmaking has resulted in the gorgeous masterpiece that is The Florida Project.
reviews.author: Kambole Campbell

reviews.text: With deep love and affection for their characters, Baker and co-writer Chris Bergoch create a vibrant community pushed to the fringes by economics but still bursting at the seams with creative possibility.
reviews.author: Glenn Heath Jr.

reviews.text: The Florida Project could easily be a Best Picture nominee this season. Baker's direction is so fluid, and the whole movie is so organic, you feel that you've lived it through it with all the characters.
reviews.author: Leah Sydney

reviews.text: The Florida Project exalts its subjects by enveloping their stories with glee and cheer, allowing them fragments of precious dignity amidst their banality or ill choices forced by survival.
reviews.author: Oggs Cruz

reviews.text: The Happiest Place on Earth can be wherever you want it to be. And I know now that should never be taken for granted.
reviews.author: Jade Budowski

reviews.text: A brilliantly dark social conscience heartbreaking comedy gem about dealing with the corruption of innocent children.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Surely [Brooklyn Pierce] will be one of Hollywood's great performers. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Lucero Calderón

reviews.text: We don't often see these people in movies, especially in American movies. We see them in the background, hustling, hawking, stealing, serving, providing - as we do in real life.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Cinema in its purest form. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ezequiel Boetti

reviews.text: It is the remarkable performance from the little Prince that propels the film forward.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: Baker follows these characters through a series of neo-realist episodes, in their absolute precariousness and in their most contagious freedom. (Complete review in newspaper Reforma, in Spanish)
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: Sean Baker's portrait of working-class Americana is powerfully narrated and beautifully performed.
reviews.author: Aakash Karkare

reviews.text: Without a trace of sentimentality, it chronicles the carefree innocence of childhood even as the children intuit that there are no easy answers to the problems they face.
reviews.author: Rashid Irani

reviews.text: [The film] achieves something very difficult and rare: the harmonious coexistence of beauty with ugliness, of the sublime with the abject. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gaspar Zimerman

reviews.text: An unusual and endearing comedy... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio Huidobro

reviews.text: With a visual language based on vignettes and with explosive colors, [director Sean] Baker builds a hilarious, exhilarating film, full of warmth and candor... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: The narrative speaks from its realism. is not frivolous and its ending is a perfect explosion of feelings. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: William Venegas

reviews.text: I rented this film mainly because of the Academy Award nomination for Willem Dafoe, who plays motel manager Bobby in this film. He is every bit as good as you would expect for such an honor, but it is the kids who steal the show in this film.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: The pathos of the film proves to be gut-wrenching
reviews.author: Dan Jardine

reviews.text: It joins Moonlight in a new pantheon of Florida-based cinema defined by harsh reality and beautiful sunsets.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: Another great Sean Baker piece that finds a way to make a heartbreaking story about poverty into a bittersweet adventure as told through through the precocious eyes of a Moonee and her mother Halley.
reviews.author: Alachia Queen

reviews.text: ...a misbegotten endeavor that's as pointless as it is infuriating.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: [Wilem] Dafoe gives a warm performance as the harassed but decent manager.
reviews.author: Boon Chan

reviews.text: Despite the sunny Florida skies, Baker shows how easily harsh realities can darken lives. The last scene of this thought-provoking film is heartrending.
reviews.author: Joanne Soh

reviews.text: ... some of the most compelling, realistic, and lovable (despite the fact that they are objectively little monsters) protagonists in any film last year.
reviews.author: Joe Reid

reviews.text: Baker has made a movie that cuts out the melodrama of after-school specials and found the profound contemplation lurking underneath.
reviews.author: David Keyes

reviews.text: Without ceasing to be political, this film is a celebration of cinema and life. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Phillipp Engel

reviews.text: "The Florida Project" is neo-realism for people who can appreciate both a Robert Rauschenberg exhibit and a Nicki Minaj video.
reviews.author: Steve Erickson

reviews.text: Non-actors Brooklynn Prince and Bria Vinaite, seconded by Willem Dafoe, simple marvel. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: ... The Florida Project is a journey to that moment where there is no turning back, where regardless of age, life has made you grow. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rafael S. Casademont

reviews.text: A little film with a big message - one of the best of 2017.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: Welcome to your favorite movie of the year. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel de Partearroyo

reviews.text: One of the best and more moving interpretations of [Willem Dafoe's] career. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Paula Arantzazu Ruiz

reviews.text: Sean Baker returns to show us in The Florida Project those characters who live in the abandoned corners of splendor, who survive as they can in a society that has forgotten them... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José Luis Forte

reviews.text: Compassionately told through the eyes of a child, [the film] is a captivating observational drama filled with moments of incredible sadness, wide-eyed innocence and pure joy.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: The film could be used as an educational tool for governments unconvinced of the importance of effective social support networks.
reviews.author: Chris Newbould

reviews.text: As he demonstrated in Tangerine, Baker has a fine way with actors. Here, he is especially good with children. Brooklynn Prince, as the six-year-old Moonee, is astonishing.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Infused with the love for the often-disregarded members of society,it's obvious that Baker has a genuine appreciation for the mistreated subjects he focuses on.
reviews.author: Alex Lines

reviews.text: An honest, accessible, compassionate account of low-rent troubles and tussles - a tale that's tender, tragic and joyous with a knockout ending that's both devastating and beautiful.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: Heir to the traditions of Huck Finn, the 'Our Gang' shorts and other tales of feral children, Sean Baker's 'Tangerine' followup transforms the strip malls and short-term motels of Disneyfied Orlando into a magical playground of discovery and peril.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: One of the year's most riveting, beautifully shot and well-acted films. It's a heartfelt look at the lives of the downtrodden.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: A reverse-Spielberg view of being a kid. No alien buddies, cuddly friends or otherworldly adventures. But there is still magic.
reviews.author: Luke Buckmaster

reviews.text: With his first three films filmmaker Sean Baker has managed to present slices of life from the underbelly of society that are often if not completely overlooked.
reviews.author: Carl Kozlowski

reviews.text: It's triumph is its determined optimism, even if it admits that is probably a fantasy. It's a tale of the fallen who, like Moonee's favourite tree, keeps on growing regardless.
reviews.author: John Bleasdale

reviews.text: The Florida Project is a remarkable movie.
reviews.author: Steve Persall

reviews.text: Beautiful and heartbreaking. Sean Baker outdoes himself with one of the best films of 2017. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Baker presents all this without poor-shaming, without being overtly political and without lecturing, but there's a real rage at the state of America -- and it's this balance that makes The Florida Project special.
Little Moonee is innocent in every sense that counts, and even her worst misdeeds are fuelled by excitement at the possibilities of life.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: A marvelous bittersweet film about the endearing naivety of childhood and the reality that gravitates around it threatening to end it all at once. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mario Alegre

reviews.text: So beautiful, heartbreaking and unassumingly masterful from beginning to end, The Florida Project is undoubtedly one of the best movies of 2017.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: An unforgettable whisper of fresh air among the stepping-stones of reality
reviews.author: Louise Keller

reviews.text: The Florida Project is a fantastic piece of writing, a showcase for a couple of breakout performances... and a film we will be hearing a lot more about as award season gets into swing.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: The world captured by Sean Baker's lens is colourful and bright, despite its impoverished inhabitants, and he never judges or pities them for their choices, even if you might. Here is a movie that shows, not tells.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Heartbreaking and humane, "The Florida Project" is one of most stirring movies you'll see this year.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: ... riveting mix of exhilaration and dread, right up to its pitch-perfect conclusion.
reviews.author: Al Hoff

reviews.text: The Florida Project is a worthy follow-up to Sean Baker's groundbreaking 2015 film Tangerine, also co-written with Chris Bergoch.
reviews.author: Vicky Roach

reviews.text: Sean Baker's dramatically infused [ethnographic] study of poverty in Kissimmee, "The Florida Project" remains a moving encapsulation of an escalating human crisis in America.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: Unique is too small a word to describe the filmmaking somersaults Sean Baker has achieved with this excellent coming of age story.
reviews.author: Damien Straker

reviews.text: Ending on an unusual note, The Florida Project may take a little time to sink in but it's a commanding character study that will hopefully open eyes.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: There isn't much of a narrative going on here, but Baker succeeds in enveloping the viewer in a very particular place.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: Enormously compassionate; joyous and funny, incisive and surprising, and truly subversive ... manages to be furious about the state of affairs in the United States while never raising its voice nor venturing near any political imagery.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: Sean Baker's latest avoids being an exploitative portrayal of poverty by empathetically portraying its characters' daily struggles, and giving time to a variety of perspectives.
reviews.author: Jake Pitre

reviews.text: A film not for the faint-hearted, easily-offended or frequently irritated by "kids these days", Florida is nonetheless a vibrant and vital slice of modern American cinema.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: The Florida Project is a funny, tragic, anarchic, hypercolour slice of life, and I loved it.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: Notably, however, Baker has no interest in making a screed against neglectful parents, poor-shaming these bedraggled families as somehow the agents of their own destruction.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: A scripted drama with the unflinching, unjudging eye of a documentary...
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: It was equal parts whimsical child fantasy and very real adult drama. It simultaneously broke my heart and opened my eyes.
reviews.author: Joshua Axelrod

reviews.text: Bittersweet and heartbreaking; words can't describe the simultaneous emotional devastation and wide-smiled happiness induced by the ending
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: A refreshing, intimate look at the kind of people that Trump voters dislike.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: One of those films that makes you feel like you're eavesdropping on others' lives. It's raw and authentic, heartbreaking and funny, profoundly humane.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: One of the greatest films of the year.
reviews.author: Sean K. Cureton

reviews.text: There's an abundance of authenticity up on the screen, which ensures that you don't know what's coming until it happens, and you don't know how hard it'll hit you until it already has.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: ... The Florida Project is a film with an abundance of heart, one which highlights and commends relentless perseverance, but which recognises that... the shiny, exciting aspects of capitalist life often work to hide its victims...
reviews.author: Sadhbh Ní Bhroin

reviews.text: The emotional payoff is so incredibly worth your time.
reviews.author: Molly Laich

reviews.text: That discovery comes slowly, but inexorably, and in Baker's talented hands, ends up feeling - at the film's end - both like an act of love ... and a punch to the heart.
reviews.author: Dan Webster

reviews.text: The Florida Project is filmmaking at its most pure; a simple story, affectingly told by characters that leave you aching.
reviews.author: Owen Richards

reviews.text: Baker's work with his largely inexperienced cast is relaxed and playful, and the film's tone is fairly assured.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: As in many of Sean Baker's films, The Florida Project's final destination doesn't quite captivate as much as the journey taken to get there.
reviews.author: James Lattimer

reviews.text: It's all about the enchantments to be found in the margins of America's moribund entertainment empire -- which makes it sound heavy, but it's not.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: The Florida Project is not a sentimental film and never fetishises its protagonists' poverty. It's oddly beautiful though, lingering over the sun-dappled highlights of a childhood that's about to go bad.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: This beautifully shot, smartly-written and wonderfully-cast drama is grim and joyful in equal measures.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: Another superbly sympathetic portrait of marginalised experience from a film-maker whose great triumph is that he never feels like a tourist. This is Moonee's world, and for a couple of hours at least, we are privileged to live in it.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: For Moonee and her friends, The Magic Castle is more than a castle-it's the Magic Kingdom.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: The audience is invited to believe that their lives are devoid of thoughts and motivations beyond hustle and pleasure, and so the movie ends up feeling like a millennial Instagram feed: cute, edgy, explosive, pithy, but shallow.
reviews.author: Cassie da Costa

reviews.text: The Magic Kingdom colors almost every scene of The Florida Project. Sean Baker's achingly beautiful and heartbreaking new film.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: This is a compassionate film about the conditions of working class America, where the next knock on the door might well be from a child welfare agency.
reviews.author: Michael Bonner

reviews.text: The camera, if especially respectful towards the children, refuses to demonise any of the characters.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: A life-affirming celebration of individuals determined to make the most of life.
reviews.author: Allan Hunter

reviews.text: One of the most memorable pictures I've seen all year.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: The combination of the worldly wise Bobby and the cheekily innocent Moonee is its charming heart.
reviews.author: Grant Rollings

reviews.text: This is a film fully attuned to the way kids find beauty all around them and Baker does remarkable work with his young cast.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: The Florida Project, director Sean Baker captures that cautious ethereality of Moonee's constructed universe against the harsh reality of transient families living in a highway motel in the shadow of The Happiest Place on Earth.
reviews.author: Brooke Corso

reviews.text: There is something real and pressing in this vision that requires us to remain attuned to the plights of people like Moonee and Halley.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: It may not be an easy piece of work to digest at times, but the emotions it's able to conjure will hit you with an unavoidable force.
reviews.author: Alex Welch

reviews.text: The Florida Project absolutely sings as a visual achievement, and not only as that.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: The Florida Project is one of the best films about childhood made anywhere in recent years.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: [It's] so simplistic and repetitious that it could have easily summed up its story as a short film, especially a documentary. Which is to say that this could have been something special in that form, and that in this form, it needed serious editing.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text: With most films you know what you are getting within the first ten minutes -- oh, it's this film; OK -- but here there are no plot points as such and we never quite know where we're headed, which gives it the thrum of real life.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: Both deeply human and sublime.
reviews.author: Rebecca Liu

reviews.text: Vibrant portrait that shows us from a child's point of view how play and enthusiasm can be ways to survive poverty.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: The film's sympathetic eye ensures it doesn't exoticise the family's plight, or dip into poverty porn. Drunken brawls, pissed-off johns and vicious catfights are simply day-to-day eruptions here, blowing in and out of the motel like the Florida weather.
reviews.author: Kate Stables

reviews.text: A summation about the power of The Florida Project feels trite - just go to see it.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: The Florida Project is a song of innocence and of experience: mainly the former.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Vibrant and brimming with vitality, this is empathic towards its subjects but fiercely critical of the system that victimises them.
reviews.author: Helen O'Hara

reviews.text: It's a celebration of the camaraderie and optimism of people whose lives could be seen from the outside as desperate or sad.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: The Florida Project is magic in the real.
reviews.author: Bill Arceneaux

reviews.text: The Florida Project is ultimately a beautiful, rough portrait of childhood set against the backdrop of the remains of the dreams of adults, which, like so many Florida oranges, have become overripe and rotten.
reviews.author: Deborah Krieger

reviews.text: For the most part what you get here are raw, non-star performances combined with knockout neon visuals.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: It's swallowed up by a style-over-substance approach increasingly at odds with its subject matter.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: Poverty and poetry, delinquency and deluxe wonder... this child's-eye view of lives on a knife-edge is terrific.
reviews.author: Jamie Graham

reviews.text: It seems more casually curious and at times even exploitative in its attempt to center the narrative of a poor, marginalized single mother and her precocious young daughter.
reviews.author: Candice Frederick

reviews.text: It's a great idea for a story that's been plucked too soon and put up on screen before the details in the script had a chance to ripen.
reviews.author: Lisa Jensen

reviews.text: There are storytelling issues that aren't resolved, but Baker largely gets by on atmosphere and periodic screen poetry, finding an original location to sort through troubled people.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: [Florida Project] is two hours of grit, outrage, and beauty.
reviews.author: Stuart Klawans

reviews.text: Transform[s] the tacky plaster eyesores despoiling the marshy landscape into almost painfully beautiful tableaux of color, lines, and ethereal fantasy.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: An astounding achievement that looks like nothing else on screens this year (Broad Street Review)
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: It's a heartbreaking world, and a hard one, set in a place that charges by the day because that's how life is lived.
reviews.author: Jay Stone

reviews.text: Sean Baker is so skilled at making ugliness appear beautiful, I'd love to turn him loose on some of my childhood photos.
reviews.author: Christopher Lawrence

reviews.text: Superb acting by the children, Bria Vinatie as Halley, and a terrific Willem Dafoe as Bobby makes a difficult film engaging. It takes courage to present this tragic struggle with poverty -- and some fortitude for the audience to confront it.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: It is at turns charming but unsettling, amusing but poignant, care-free but thought-provoking. But the real story here is Brooklynn Prince, a 6-year-old star in the making.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: ...finds the beauty in a scruffy part of Florida that the tourist board would probably prefer that you ignore.
reviews.author: Sarah Boslaugh

reviews.text: ... a funny, gut-wrenching, emotionally complex masterwork of the human condition that exudes warmth and humility in every frame.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Quite simply, one of the best films about childhood ever made.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: You'll weep for these kids and try to hope for their future.
reviews.author: Jeff Simon

reviews.text: It heads any list of the best films of the year by a substantial margin.
reviews.author: M. Faust

reviews.text: Frankly, today, what six-year old do you see walking around without a parent? Social Services would be called immediately.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: The Florida Project, though, dances deftly around kitchen-sink realism and instead looks at this pastel world through the eyes of characters too young to know, or care, that they aren't rich.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: Sleazy and shrill, it exploits the bleak, anti-social underbelly of economic inequality around The Magic Kingdom - emerging as perhaps the most depressing film of the year.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Your heart will break, but it will also swell.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: Mr. Dafoe turns in his best, most touching performance in years.
reviews.author: Barry Paris

reviews.text: Never before have I seen [Dafoe] display the particular emotions that he displays in this film.
reviews.author: Dan Grossman

reviews.text: I can't think of a movie that better captures the evanescent joy and freedom of childhood than The Florida Project.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: A wonderfully humane, heartbreakingly kind film.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: One of the most transcendent big-screen stories of the year comes in the pint-sized package of Moonee (Brooklynn Kimberly Prince).
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: Youngsters named Moonee (the divine Brooklynn Prince), Scooty and Jancey become those mischievous and usually unsupervised little rascals all over again.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: How can one of the most joyful films of the year also be one of the saddest?
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: [Director Sean Baker's] frantic depiction of Moonee's final fantasy verges on both brilliance and heartbreak.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: The best, most heartbreakingly inspiring film of the year.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: [Brooklyn] Prince-with considerable help from her costars, Baker, and screenwriter Chris Bergoch-resonates beyond the twee and cute. At the film's climax, Prince delivers a performance that would make even the surliest curmudgeon cry.
reviews.author: Chase Burns

reviews.text: Director Sean Baker's sun-drenched, pastel-colored drama has a vibrant energy even amid the most heartbreaking moments
reviews.author: Mara Reinstein

reviews.text: It's one of the most effective, honest portraits of childhood you'll ever see, and a touching, poignant snapshot of American life in 2017.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: The Florida Project is painfully good. [Sean] Baker has arrived.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: The world of The Florida Project feels tangible, lyrical, forbidding and magical all at once, a boundaryless playground for kids and a quicksand prison for everyone else.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: ... a truly magnificent effort from director Sean Baker and cowriter Chris Bergoch.
reviews.author: Ken Eisner

reviews.text: You feel as if you've slipped inside of Moonee's enchanted world, while at the same time seeing the harsh reality of Halley's. That contrast is devastating, right up to a final sequence that's sure to break your heart in two.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: The Florida Project is certainly lively, but it is anything but redemptive. In spite of its episodic documentary quality, it traces an overdetermined downward spiral.
reviews.author: J. Hoberman

reviews.text: Sean Baker's effortlessly headlong dive into a child's imagination is a tender thunderclap... generous, grand, gorgeous... ground-level magic.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: Director Sean Baker's luminous odyssey overflows with wit and joy.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: The Florida Project is a poetic mass of contradictions, a delicately graceful and harrowingly gritty drama that presents an innocent child's-eye view of a troubled adult world, a place of heartbreak and poverty in the shadow of the Magic Kingdom.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Baker places no dramatic emphasis on any individual scene, granting a sense of wide-eyed wonder to major and minor events alike.
reviews.author: Ben Sachs

reviews.text: Rarely has such a heartbreakingly innocent portrait of childhood been portrayed on film.
reviews.author: Laura DeMarco

reviews.text: Undeniably essential viewing.
reviews.author: Ryan Morris

reviews.text: The performances by the children, especially (Brooklyn) Prince, are magical and unforgettable. You will think of them long after you leave the theater.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: The fluid visuals are a perfect match for the curiosity and exuberance of the kids, who prowl the motel grounds and beyond on the hunt for mischief.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: Baker never succumbs to the sirens of miserabilism. Instead, he prefers the fanciful fantasy of the children who, in their flight forward, can glean moments of happiness for themselves from the simple light of a blue sky.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: A three-dimensional microcosm of the millions of families denied their share of the American dream by a corrupt system that tends to only reward the rich.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: This is a story told with authenticity and power, helped along by its cast of newcomers.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: The Florida Project, despite its ability to marvel at the natural wonders that offset poverty-stricken circumstances, doesn't sugarcoat harsh realities.
reviews.author: Stephen Schaefer

reviews.text: For all that kitschy beauty, I wouldn't want to spend one more minute with Moonee, here or anywhere else.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: One surprising thing about The Florida Project is how rife it is with hope, even as it's weighed down by the hapless, unsustainable situation of its protagonists.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: These people aren't living the American dream. They're barely making do. But still, The Florida Project suggests that our most precious relationships are held together with some undefinable, beautiful glue.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: It's film that'll make you wince at times, and you'll most likely not want to see twice, but seeing it once is an experience you'll not soon forget.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: This movie puts the wild, comic tales of resourceful poor kids into a frame, pulling back just enough to make it clear that the situation Moonee's in - while exciting - is untenable.
reviews.author: Noel Murray

reviews.text: The Florida Project is not just a downer, although parts of it are harrowing. The young lead actors are funny and vivacious, speaking with unaffected charisma and honesty.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: Alexis Zabe's rapturous cinematography reminds us that magic is where you find it. You don't need a golden ticket to Mickey's kingdom, although you can see it from here.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Baker has made a surprisingly joyous film from this despairing situation...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: As Bobby, the saintly, suffering bastard who keeps order, Dafoe is like a new man.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: The sun-washed reality of The Florida Project, which concludes with a touch of poetry that might break you in two. It's not a happy ending, but it is, like the rest of the film, pretty much perfect.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Dafoe delivers his finest performance in recent memory, bringing to levelheaded, unsanctimonious life a character who offers a glimmer of hope and caring within a world markedly short on both.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: The Florida Project may seem to have more episodes than a narrative through line, but that seems also true to the occupants of the Magic Kingdom, who believe they're simply in a transitional state while they're actually stuck in idle.
reviews.author: Marjorie Baumgarten

reviews.text: Its humanist depiction of families on the fringe of society - an experience that is too often erased from the narrative we tell ourselves about the place where we live - makes it essential viewing.
reviews.author: Thaddeus McCollum

reviews.text: Dafoe has never had a role this warm and sweet, and he plays it for low-keyed honesty. The kids and the adults, some non-professionals, all become part of a bright purple beehive.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Rarely in a movie will you want a character to succeed more than Moonee. Yet Baker doesn't sugarcoat the odds, which, despite eventual moments of real magic, remain long indeed.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: It may be impossible to overstate just how wonderful Willem Dafoe is in this film.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: "The Florida Project" is - in nerve, guts, heart, and mind - one of the finest films of 2017.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: ... perfectly set up and disappointingly executed story about down-on-their-luck folks who call a motel in Orlando home.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: The Florida Project is perceptive to the charm and strength of character you can find in humble places.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: Dafoe's performance as Bobby is superb, a guardian angel for the 21st century.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: Baker & Bergoch's examination of the low class and welfare lifestyle in Florida is eye opening and at times hard to watch.
reviews.author: Stephanie Archer

reviews.text: A tattered tale about kids growing up in an American economy barely afloat offshore Florida's signature tourism mecca, making their own magic in the shadow of the Magic Kingdom.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: These characters are the detritus left behind by a 21st-century America with increasingly less room for the poor and undereducated. The Florida Project never looks at them with pity, only understanding and sympathy.
reviews.author: Stephen Danay

reviews.text: The impression is a disturbing film of energy and compassion that left me with an inescapable sadness, from which director Baker offers no way out.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: As it stands, there's a greatness in it, but also stretches of emptiness. Still, this is an original piece of work, and no one who sees it will forget it.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: The Florida Project represents a new low in class condescension. . .[Director] Baker loves irresponsible, antisocial types, and his method is similarly undisciplined.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: The Florida Project is tonally playful while in fact being a wondrously sad piece of art.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: Nothing "HAPPENS" in "The Florida Project" but lots of stuff "happens" as we live with Moonee, her mom and her friends in a world that is both modern and retro at once.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: There is no other film quite like it, this year or any other.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Willem Dafoe knows from tortured roles (Platoon, The Last Temptation of Christ), but this creation -- a delicate blend of protector, fusspot and secret survivor -- is his richest, most lovable piece of work.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: This is a deeply humanist filmmaker, and he's sympathetic to these characters, flaws and all.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: Few movies about children capture the very essence of youth, the precious intersection of innocence and wonder that so often co-exists along the margins of a darker reality.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: The Florida Project is spattered with profound sadness, with moments of externalized, violent frustration at presumed helplessness, at practically being born into all this.
reviews.author: Kyle Turner

reviews.text: Baker has imbued this whole terrific movie with a child's sense of discovery - the sort that can turn a decrepit, pastel corner of Orlando into a vibrant cinematic playground.
reviews.author: Bob Mondello

reviews.text: It is because Baker views the world without blinders that the moments of lyricism in The Florida Project are so piercing. When a rainbow shows up in the sky, it's not just a rainbow; it's a benediction.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: The film ends on a fantastical note that is jarring in its change in tone, yet provocative in what it has to say...a humanistic work of art that lingers.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: The Florida Project is eye-opening, unconventional, sweet, scary, odd and heartbreaking. It's a fantastic movie, one I haven't stopped thinking about since I saw it.
reviews.author: Sean O'Connell

reviews.text: ...a triumphant exercise in cinematic empathy that also serves as a subversive societal challenge.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: ...a style of filmmaking that feels almost like an Errol Morris documentary ("Vernon, Florida" comes to mind). It's pretty magical.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: The Florida Project is one of this year's best films, a remarkable slice of life. If ever there were a sleeper deserving of wide recognition, this is it.
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: The Florida Project is by no stretch an easy watch, but it's an incredibly rewarding one.
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: Dafoe's sensitive performance anchors the movie's slippery adult world, and Baker builds a cinematic mood beautifully; the strip malls and swampland and buzzing cicadas on screen feel as real and tactile as the theater seat beneath you.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: Though Moonee's story may not have a Hollywood happy ending when she's grown and the world has been cruel, Baker has created an indomitable character who's at least got a fighting chance.
reviews.author: April Wolfe

reviews.text: It is impossible not to fall a little bit in love with The Florida Project.
reviews.author: Gregory Wakeman

reviews.text: The Florida Project achieves something rare and magical: presenting existence from the perspective of a young child while, at the same time, providing enough "clues" that viewers are able to decipher what's really going on.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: All childhoods must come to an end, few of them as piercingly as the one in "The Florida Project," Sean Baker's raw, exuberant and utterly captivating new movie.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: As in previous films, Mr. Baker mixes amateur and professional actors to exceptional effect.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Director Sean Baker crafts one of the best and toughest films about childhood ever and gives a never-better Willem Dafoe a clear shot at an Oscar.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: To balance joy and desperation as gracefully as Mr. Baker does - to interweave giddiness and heartbreak - is no easy feat.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: Written and directed with rich texture by Sean Baker, The Florida Project, which just debuted at the New York Film Festival ahead of its release this week in theaters, is the latest in a vivid, intensely naturalistic new subgenre of white-trash cinema.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: The pleasure of The Florida Project is that we lose ourselves in Moonee's Eden: its aesthetics; its logic.
reviews.author: Julia Felsenthal

reviews.text: The Florida Project is both radiant and unsentimental.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: ... Dafoe's warm and generous performance is simply astonishing.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: This is a film of rare joy, even in its more unsparing moments, and the kind of film that should be seen by anybody who loves movies.
reviews.author: Dominick Suzanne-Mayer

reviews.text: Sean Baker's beautiful heartbreaker scratches just below the cheery lilac and bubblegum pink to expose the layers of privation festering in this sunshiny state.
reviews.author: Elizabeth Weitzman

reviews.text: Sean Baker's latest is a melancholy slice of wonder, viewed through our pint sized protagonist's eyes.
reviews.author: Jacob Knight

reviews.text: The Florida Project lights us onto an authentic perspective, never shying away from the grime and sorrow of its world, but never making it the film's unyielding focal point, either.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: Baker's neo-realistic eye for humour, honesty and heartbreak has crafted a slow burn, potent commentary on America's struggling underclass.
reviews.author: Simon Foster

reviews.text: While Baker's previous movie, Tangerine, is a milestone in LGBTQ filmmaking, The Florida Project doesn't ring as true to life.
reviews.author: Valerie Complex

reviews.text: Sean Baker's rollicking movie about kids running loose in a rundown Florida hotel starts as colorful entertainment and ends up as a portrait of how people fall through the cracks in modern America.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: "The Florida Project's" great find is Bria Vinaite, who seems to run the line between Taryn Manning's work in "Hustle & Flow" and Elisabeth Shue's hooker with a heart of gold in "Leaving Las Vegas."
reviews.author: Clayton Davis

reviews.text: When Florida Project works, it works beautifully, but one never quite shakes the nagging feeling that this insistence on finding joy and momentary pleasure amidst hopelessness is the province of storytellers more privileged than their precarious subjects.
reviews.author: Angelo Muredda

reviews.text: When it hits, like a sudden thunderstorm after heat wave, the impact is astounding.
reviews.author: Brian D. Johnson

reviews.text: As Moonee, Brooklynn Prince is a revelation. There's not a single artificial note in her performance, just raw charm.
reviews.author: Angie Han

reviews.text: The story seems to be armed only with trivial vignettes, although I must confess that the protagonist's charisma ends up winning over the audience. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Oscar Uriel

reviews.text: Underneath the vibrancy of Moonee's spirit, Baker delivers a heavy-handed statement about the fraudulent hopes offered by Disney magic, and the way so many American dreams have been shattered.
reviews.author: Caryn James

reviews.text: You come away better for having known this crew, a demographic that's sorely underrepresented on the screen.
reviews.author: Sara Stewart

reviews.text: The Florida Project is one of this year's most warm, vibrant films.
reviews.author: Shane Slater

reviews.text: Sean Baker spends much of the film investing the minutia of the down-and-out lives within this little ecosystem with a bittersweet energy and significance.
reviews.author: Ed Gonzalez

reviews.text: A film of small notes that combine to form something major, the kind of movie that sneaks up on you and sticks with you
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: A magnificent look at the freewheeling wonder of childhood.
reviews.author: Oliver Whitney

reviews.text: A wonderful piece of filmmaking.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: Vividly shot in 35mm, The Florida Project continues Baker's insightful chronicling of society's underbelly.
reviews.author: Paul Ennis

reviews.text: [Sean] Baker mostly crafts a tiny adventure of absorbing wonder.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Sean Baker once again pulls us into a world we never thought we could fall in love with.
reviews.author: David Noh

reviews.text: Bring Advil. You'll need it.
reviews.author: Kent Turner

reviews.text: The Florida Project won't let us look away. Nor, given its brilliance, would we want to. Instead, we laugh, we watch silently, and we're challenged to stop simplifying people's lives so we can offer easy theoretical answers.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: Frenzied, colourful and heart-breaking, Sean Baker's The Florida Project is a remarkable feat of filmmaking.
reviews.author: Joseph Walsh

reviews.text: In an era with remarkable child actors in films such as 'Room' and 'Moonlight', Baker's ability to siphon such authentic performances is truly a marvel.
reviews.author: Gregory Ellwood

reviews.text: Steeped in glorious colour under the warm glow of a Florida sun, Sean Baker's The Florida Project is as indelible and warm as it looks.
reviews.author: Jo-Ann Titmarsh

reviews.text: Indeed, this struggle can feel like real life at times so it's a shame that no apparent effort has been made by the director to give the viewer cause to empathize.
reviews.author: Rory O'Connor

reviews.text: Beautiful, vibrant, heartfelt and hilarious.
reviews.author: David Jenkins

reviews.text: Sean Baker's follow-up to TANGERINE is a triumph on many levels.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: The Florida Project is very much its own pink plastic beast. It is one of the great films about childhood.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: A film with its own universe and fascinating, and a complaint - without underlining. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Baker establish an antithetical parallelism between the concept of happiness of the first world children and the one of the misfits. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Sáez Villarino

reviews.text: The Florida Project is a work in a state of grace. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Àngel Quintana

reviews.text: Baker offers little hope, and the only certainty is that childhood, and innocence, always have an expiration date. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Ruiz

reviews.text: The Florida Project completely turns the American dream and shows us the devastated backyard of Donald Trump's tacky America. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos F. Heredero

reviews.text: The off-kilter, unusual, matter-of-fact observations from a very young child bring a fresh perspective, realism and humour to well-worn territory that too often drowns in pity, sentiment or demonisation.
reviews.author: Isabel Stevens

reviews.text: A truthful and sublimely bittersweet slice of life, tracing celebratory highs and lamentable lows on the outer economic edges of the Sunshine State.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: A remarkable study of poverty, family and personal responsibility, The Florida Project meticulously illustrates how life on the margins affects one impressionable six-year-old.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: As a filmmaker, Baker is a graceful neorealist voyeur who thrives on improvisation, and his storytelling, in The Florida Project, is mostly just a series of anecdotes. But that turns out to be enough.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: Things look grim for Halley and Moonee, but we can expect a lot from the people who brought their marvelous story to light.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: The Florida Project further cements Baker's status as one of the most innovative American directors working today, but he's also an essential advocate for the stories this country often doesn't get to see.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: The deceptive intelligence of The Florida Project is how immersive this bouncy-castle reality is while sitting exactly on top of the drawn-out, unremarked tragedy that is life on the margins of respectable, solvent society.
reviews.author: Jessica Kiang

reviews.text: A fabulous mosaic of one particular pocket of America's invisible homeless population - families living hand-to-mouth in motels originally designed to catch the tourist overspill from the flashy theme-park resorts across town.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: [A] brilliant, buoyant, and ultimately heart-wrenching film.
reviews.author: Emily Yoshida

synopsis: Set in the shadow of the most magical place on Earth, 6-year-old Moonee and her two best friends forge their own adventures, while Moonee's struggling mom and a kindhearted motel manager protect the kids from the harsh reality that surrounds them.
